scenarioStory.history: Husband reports his wife was gardening when she suddenly stopped mid-sentence, dropped her trowel, and could not lift her right arm. She has not spoken a clear word since. He immediately called 911; time from last seen normal to the call was about 15 minutes.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 66-year-old female with acute right-sided weakness, facial droop, and expressive aphasia witnessed by her husband approximately 15 minutes ago. → Stroke scale performed, LKW established: Crew completes a validated stroke scale confirming a positive finding, checks blood glucose to rule out a stroke mimic, and documents a precise last-known-well time within the thrombolytic window. → LVO suspected, thrombectomy center notified: With a positive severity scale suggesting possible large vessel occlusion, the crew minimizes scene time, avoids treating the elevated blood pressure, and transports directly to a thrombectomy-capable stroke center with early notification.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Sudden right-sided weakness and inability to speak

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 66-year-old female with acute right-sided weakness, facial droop, and expressive aphasia witnessed by her husband approximately 15 minutes ago.

scenarioEvents.name: Stroke scale performed, LKW established
scenarioEvents.description: Crew completes a validated stroke scale confirming a positive finding, checks blood glucose to rule out a stroke mimic, and documents a precise last-known-well time within the thrombolytic window.
relatedChecklist: Perform validated prehospital stroke scale (facial droop, arm drift, speech) — positive for all three
Check blood glucose to rule out hypoglycemia as a stroke mimic (result 132 mg/dL, no treatment needed)
Establish precise last-known-well time from husband (15 minutes prior to EMS arrival)
Do not treat elevated blood pressure in the field

scenarioEvents.name: LVO suspected, thrombectomy center notified
scenarioEvents.description: With a positive severity scale suggesting possible large vessel occlusion, the crew minimizes scene time, avoids treating the elevated blood pressure, and transports directly to a thrombectomy-capable stroke center with early notification.
relatedChecklist: Elevate head of stretcher 15-30 degrees with neck neutral; protect the weak right arm
Notify thrombectomy-capable stroke center early with LKW time and positive severity scale findings

scenarioEvents.name: Blood pressure treated in the field
scenarioEvents.description: The crew attempts to lower the patient's elevated blood pressure out of concern for stroke severity, contrary to protocol. This risks dropping cerebral perfusion pressure to the ischemic penumbra and worsening the neurologic deficit.
relatedChecklist: Recognize inappropriate BP treatment; resume permissive hypertension and expedite transport
